summary: Add a clear explanation and targeted practice for the ionic-radius pattern across a period, which the current note and questions treat only as separate ion comparisons.

improvements.where: note, after the Radius trends paragraph in ## Key ideas
improvements.why: Outcome 9701-1.1.7 asks for variation in ionic radius across a period and down a group; the note gives atomic trends and isolated cation/anion comparisons but does not connect these into the ionic trend.
improvements.what: Add a short explanation that ionic radii of comparable cations decrease across a period as nuclear charge increases for the same electron shell, then rise sharply on moving to anions because the stable anions have an additional occupied shell; comparable ions increase down a group as another shell is added. Use Period 3 examples such as $\ce{Na+}$, $\ce{Mg^2+}$, $\ce{P^3-}$ and $\ce{S^2-}$, and make clear that a simple monotonic trend does not apply across the cation-to-anion boundary. Paraphrase the learner's source.

improvements.why: Current radius questions test atomic trends, single-ion changes and isoelectronic comparisons, but do not ask learners to explain the cation-to-anion jump or the ionic trend down a group.
improvements.what: Add one exam-style explain item on the Period 3 ionic-radius discontinuity and one compare/explain item on comparable ions down a group; include a misconception distractor or rubric point that checks shell count before nuclear charge.
